findings.title: A device or tab that has not reloaded erases a finished lesson just by opening its Watch step (whole-record last-writer-wins)
findings.detail: put() rebuilds a record from THIS device's copy ({...state[coll][id], ...patch, t: now}) and merge() in both files keeps whichever whole record has the larger t. Player calls onSegment on its very first show(), so merely opening Watch writes {seg, t: now}. Sequence: phone loads the page in the morning (sees only guess); laptop finishes lesson 1-1 (watched, quiz, done, recall) and syncs; evening, the phone tab is still open and the learner taps the lesson. The phone's record {guess, seg:0, t: later} wins on the server, and the laptop's next page load replaces its own finished record with it. The lesson is no longer done anywhere: percent complete drops, its field-guide entry and drill lock again, review cards stay but the lesson shows as next up. Nothing tells the learner. The same happens to settings (one object, last writer wins) and to any lesson touched on two devices. The client only pulls from the server at page load and after its own pushes, so a long-lived phone tab is always stale.
findings.evidence: node qa/site_review_scratch/store_tests.mjs (the real store.js, one module instance per simulated device, against the real worker.js, with a controllable clock) section 2: server after the laptop finished 1-1 = {guess, watched, quiz, done, recall}; after the phone merely opened Watch = {guess:2, seg:0}; laptop after its next load = {guess:2, seg:0}; stats.done 1 -> 0.
findings.fix: Merge per field, not per record, in ONE shared function used by worker.js and store.js: for lessons keep done/watched/quiz/guess/recall from whichever side has them (earliest done, best or latest quiz), take seg from the newer side; for cards keep the record with the larger n (tie: newer t); for settings merge key by key with a timestamp per key. Do not write seg on the first show() of a Player (only when the part actually changes or playback starts). Re-fetch /api/progress when the tab becomes visible again and merge before the next put.

findings.title: 'Start over' erases everything on a double-click, on every device, with no undo
findings.detail: The same button arms and confirms: the first click sets data-sure and changes the label, the second click on the same spot calls store.resetAll(). A double-click (or Enter held on the focused button, or two taps) delivers both clicks before the changed label can be read. resetAll() replaces the state with a reset timestamp, pushes it, and merge() then deletes every record older than it on the server and on every other device at its next sync. There is no confirmation dialog, no delay, no undo, and the daily backup does not get it back (next finding).
findings.evidence: By reading app.js:363 and store.js:125 (no browser was allowed). The irreversible part is executed: node qa/site_review_scratch/worker_tests.mjs (the real worker.js fetch handler in-process, in-memory KV) -> 'backup after same-day reset' and 'restore then next sync' both end with lessons: [].
findings.fix: Make the second step a different, deliberate action: e.g. after the first click show an inline panel that says what will be erased, with a text field that must contain ERASE (or a button that only enables after 3 seconds) and a Cancel. Drop the armed state after 10 seconds. Before sending a reset, have the worker write an extra undated backup (key backup:<user>:before-reset-<ts>, no TTL), and offer 'Undo' for a minute (keep the old state in memory and push it back with fresh timestamps and the reset removed).

findings.title: 'Start from the beginning' never plays: the stage shows Pause but there is no sound (or the first part runs on the silent clock)
findings.detail: The button runs this.show(0, false); this.play(). show() is async and only swaps audio.src after an await, so play() starts the OLD clip (the resume part), and one microtask later show() replaces src with part 0 and, because autoplay is false, never calls play() again. Outcome A (clip was already loaded, the normal case): player.playing is true, the button shows Pause, the audio element is paused on part 0 - nothing happens until the learner presses Pause and then Play. Outcome B (clip still loading): the interrupted play() rejects with AbortError, the catch treats that as a missing clip and calls goSilent(), and part 0 advances on the silent clock with captions and reveals but no narration.
findings.evidence: node qa/site_review_scratch/player_tests.mjs (the real player.js in Node on a minimal fake DOM and a fake audio element that follows the HTML rules for play()/pause()/src: a pending play() promise rejects with AbortError when src changes or pause() is called). No real browser was used, so the browser half is by specification, the player half is executed code. Scenario A: 'clip already loaded: i=0 playing=true silent=false clock=false audio.paused=true'; 'clip still loading: i=0 playing=true silent=true clock=true audio.paused=true'.
findings.fix: onclick: () => this.show(0, true)   (show() already calls play() after it has set the new src). In general never call play() right after an un-awaited show().

findings.title: Audio is served without byte-range support on the real runtime; the local harness hides it by faking 206 responses
findings.detail: env.ASSETS.fetch(req) on workerd answers a request with 'Range: bytes=0-99' (and 'bytes=100-') with 200, the full 183,525-byte body and no Accept-Ranges/Content-Range. build/dev_server.mjs implements Range itself ('browsers ask for audio in ranges'), so every local test saw 206. Safari on iPhone/iPad/Mac probes media with a Range request and is documented to require range support for audio and video; without it clips can fail to load (the player then silently falls back to its reading-pace clock, so a lesson would 'play' with no sound on the phone) or load without seeking. The drills are single 1.6-2.7 MB files of 4-6 minutes whose slider and +/-15s buttons set currentTime: in Chrome a seek past what has downloaded has to wait for the whole file, in Safari it may not work at all. Whether production Cloudflare adds range handling in front of the Worker could not be tested from here.
findings.evidence: Run before the memory limit stopped it: the real worker under local workerd (wrangler 4.166.0 dev, config qa/site_review_scratch/wrangler.jsonc, port 8799) probed with curl. 'curl -H "range: bytes=0-99" /audio/1-1/01-5caffdbac18180.mp3' -> 'HTTP/1.1 200 OK, Content-Length: 183525', no Content-Range; the asset worker bundle shipped in node_modules/miniflare has no Range handling. NOT confirmed: the behaviour of iOS Safari and of the production edge - test one lesson and one drill on the phone right after deploy.
findings.fix: Answer ranges in the worker for audio: if (req.headers.has('range') && res.status === 200 && path.endsWith('.mp3')) { const buf = await res.arrayBuffer(); const m = /^bytes=(\d*)-(\d*)$/.exec(req.headers.get('range')); if (m) { const size = buf.byteLength; let start = m[1] ? +m[1] : size - +m[2], end = m[1] && m[2] ? Math.min(+m[2], size - 1) : size - 1; if (start >= size || start > end) return new Response(null, { status: 416, headers: { 'content-range': 'bytes */' + size } }); h.set('content-range', 'bytes ' + start + '-' + end + '/' + size); h.set('content-length', String(end - start + 1)); h.set('accept-ranges', 'bytes'); return new Response(buf.slice(start, end + 1), { status: 206, headers: h }); } }  and set accept-ranges: bytes on the plain 200. Add a wrangler dev run to the pre-deploy check so harness-only behaviour cannot hide this again.

findings.title: A lesson can never be marked done if the questions are finished before the video's last second
findings.detail: done is set only inside the quiz's finish(), and only if watched is already set; watching to the end (onComplete, line 174) sets watched but never done. watched is set only when the last part ends or Next is pressed on it. A learner who clicks the Check tab during the last part (all five tabs are always clickable), or who leaves a lesson whose audio stalled, answers the four questions and gets 'All four. Solid.' - but the record has quiz and no done. Going back and watching to the end adds watched and still no done. The lesson stays 'Next up' on the home page, the module bar and percent complete do not move, its field-guide entry and the module drill stay locked. The only way out is to redo the quiz after watching, which nothing suggests.
findings.evidence: node qa/site_review_scratch/store_tests.mjs (the real store.js, one module instance per simulated device, against the real worker.js, with a controllable clock) section 8 (finish() and onComplete copied verbatim from app.js): after the quiz {guess, seg:7, quiz}; after then watching to the end {guess, seg:0, quiz, watched} -> done: false.
findings.fix: Compute completion in one place and call it from both ends: const settle = () => { const s = lessonState(id); if (!s.done && s.quiz && s.watched) store.put('lessons', id, { done: Date.now() }); }; call settle() at the end of finish() and of onComplete. (Or decide that finishing the questions is what completes a lesson and drop the watched condition; see also the '|| true' finding, which already lets Next mark a lesson watched without playing it.)

findings.title: Client clocks are trusted: a reset or record stamped in the future silently deletes later work; a device whose clock runs fast overrides newer progress
findings.detail: reset = max(a.reset, b.reset) is sticky and every record with t < reset is deleted in every merge, on the server and on each device. (1) 'Start over' on a device whose clock is ahead by X (or any PUT carrying settings.reset in the future): everything recorded by correctly-set devices during the next X is deleted at each sync, with a 200 response. With reset one year ahead the account stays empty for a year. (2) A record written with t far in the future can never be updated again. (3) Ordinary skew: a phone running 2 hours fast writes {seg:3}; twenty minutes later the laptop finishes that lesson; the laptop's own sync replaces its finished record with the phone's older one because the phone's t is larger.
findings.evidence: node qa/site_review_scratch/worker_tests.mjs (the real worker.js fetch handler in-process, in-memory KV): 'future-dated reset' -> lessonsRightAfter [], lessonsAfterNewWorkFromHealthyDevice [], resetStuckAt 2027-11-21; 'record with a far-future t can never be updated' -> {done:1, t:9e15}. node qa/site_review_scratch/store_tests.mjs (the real store.js, one module instance per simulated device, against the real worker.js, with a controllable clock) section 3: laptop record {watched, quiz, done} becomes {seg:3} after its own sync; 30 min after a reset on the fast phone the laptop's new lesson and card are gone.
findings.fix: In the worker, clamp on the way in: const now = Date.now(); any incoming t or settings.t or settings.reset greater than now + 5 min is set to now (and a reset that was clamped is applied as 'now'). Return the server time in every /api/progress response and let store.js keep an offset (serverNow - Date.now()) that it adds to every timestamp it writes.

findings.title: The daily backup does not rescue an accidental reset: same-day work is not in it, and a restored copy is deleted again at the next sync
findings.detail: The backup is the state BEFORE the first PUT of each UTC day, written once. A reset later that day leaves a backup without anything done that day, and tomorrow's backup is already the empty state. Restoring by hand (wrangler kv key put progress:owner <backup>) does not work either: every browser still holds settings.reset in localStorage and sends it with its next PUT, merge() takes the max and deletes all restored records again (their t is older than the reset). There is no restore endpoint or UI, 'Download a copy' has no matching import, and backups are only reachable with wrangler.
findings.evidence: node qa/site_review_scratch/worker_tests.mjs (the real worker.js fetch handler in-process, in-memory KV): 'backup after same-day reset' -> backupHolds [1-1], lostEvenWithBackup [1-2, 1-3]; 'restore then next sync' -> lessons [].
findings.fix: Write a backup immediately before applying any incoming reset that is newer than the stored one (separate key, long TTL). Add POST /api/progress/restore?day=YYYY-MM-DD that loads the backup, removes settings.reset, restamps every record with the server's now and stores it; expose it in Settings together with an 'Import a copy' that does the same with the downloaded file.

findings.title: A push that fails while the tab is being hidden is never retried, the tab does not re-sync when it comes back, and the badge still means little
findings.detail: visibilitychange->hidden calls push(true); push() clears the pending timer first, and on failure only re-schedules when keepalive is false. So the common phone flow - finish the questions, switch app, the request dies on a flaky network or a 5xx - leaves the change in localStorage only, with no timer. Coming back to the tab does nothing (the listener only handles 'hidden'); the next attempt is the next put(), an 'online' event or a full reload. If the learner then continues on the laptop it starts from stale state, which is exactly the precondition of the record-overwrite finding. Related: the header badge shows 'Synced' whenever online !== false, including before the first sync has finished and while a push is pending (up to 20 s for position updates).
findings.evidence: node qa/site_review_scratch/store_tests.mjs (the real store.js, one module instance per simulated device, against the real worker.js, with a controllable clock) section 4: after the failed keepalive push 'timers pending: []', syncStatus online:false; after returning to the tab 'timers [] | server has 1-1: false'; an ordinary failed push schedules [30000].
findings.fix: catch { online = false; dirty = true; if (!keepalive) schedulePush(30000); } and addEventListener('visibilitychange', () => { if (document.visibilityState === 'visible') refresh(); }) where refresh() GETs /api/progress, merges, and pushes if dirty or different. Give the badge three states: 'Saving...' while a timer or request is pending, 'Synced' after a 200, 'Saved on this device' after a failure.

findings.title: Any interrupted play() is treated as 'clip missing', so pressing Play/Pause quickly or Next twice switches a healthy lesson to the silent clock
findings.detail: play() does audio.play().catch(e => e.name === 'NotAllowedError' ? pause() : goSilent()). A play() promise also rejects with AbortError when pause() is called or src changes before playback has started - both routine. (1) Slow network or a double tap: Play then Pause before the clip starts -> silent = true; the next Play runs startClock() and never touches the audio element: captions and reveals advance, no narration, for the rest of that part. (2) Next pressed twice quickly, ArrowRight held (key repeat), or dragging the scrubber across parts while playing: the first part's pending play() is aborted by the second src change -> goSilent() -> the clock runs while the audio element also plays; timeupdate is ignored, and after a Pause the Play button restarts only the clock (audio stays paused). The learner gets a lesson that looks alive and is mute, with no message.
findings.evidence: node qa/site_review_scratch/player_tests.mjs (the real player.js in Node on a minimal fake DOM and a fake audio element that follows the HTML rules for play()/pause()/src: a pending play() promise rejects with AbortError when src changes or pause() is called). No real browser was used, so the browser half is by specification, the player half is executed code. Scenario B: after play+pause 'silent=true'; after pressing Play again 'playing=true silent=true clock=true audio.paused=true'. Scenario C: 200 ms after two quick Nexts 'silent=true clock=true audio.paused=false'; after pause + play 'clock=true audio.paused=true'.
findings.fix: Only real load failures may switch to the clock: const token = this.token; this.audio.play().catch((e) => { if (token !== this.token || e.name === 'AbortError') return; if (e.name === 'NotAllowedError') this.pause(); else this.goSilent(); }); keep the 'error' listener for genuine failures but ignore it when audio.error is null or the src is empty, and show a small 'Audio unavailable - reading pace' note in the controls whenever silent is true for a part that has a src.

findings.title: Media-key handlers and drill audio outlive their views: a headset Play restarts a lesson that was left, drills keep playing under a lesson and cannot be paused from the headset
findings.detail: (1) destroy() does not clear the four navigator.mediaSession action handlers, so they keep pointing at the destroyed Player for the rest of the page session. A headset or lock-screen Play then calls its play(): destroy() had set src = '' (error -> silent), so the clock starts on the detached player, and at the end of that part show(i+1, true) loads the next clip and really plays it - narration from a lesson the learner left, on whatever page they are on - while onSegment keeps writing seg to the store and onComplete can mark the lesson watched. (2) audioCard() (new drill player) creates Audio objects that are never attached to the document; el.stop() is defined but never called and route() only destroys the lesson Player. Leaving #/drills leaves the drill playing with no control on screen; opening a lesson and pressing Play overlays both narrations. document.querySelectorAll('audio') in the card's click handler finds nothing, because neither kind of audio is in the DOM. (3) Because of (1), after any lesson has been opened the headset Pause calls the dead Player's pause() instead of pausing the drill - on the 'On the move?' feature whose main control is the headset.
findings.evidence: node qa/site_review_scratch/player_tests.mjs (the real player.js in Node on a minimal fake DOM and a fake audio element that follows the HTML rules for play()/pause()/src: a pending play() promise rejects with AbortError when src changes or pause() is called). No real browser was used, so the browser half is by specification, the player half is executed code. Scenario E: 'mediaSession handlers still registered after destroy(): play,pause,previoustrack,nexttrack'; 1.1 s after the media key 'i=1 playing=true audio.paused=false src=seg1.mp3 | onSegment calls since destroy: 1 | wrap.isConnected: false'. (2) and (3) by reading: grep shows el.stop is assigned at app.js:54 and never called.
findings.fix: destroy(): for (const a of ['play','pause','previoustrack','nexttrack']) navigator.mediaSession?.setActionHandler(a, null); navigator.mediaSession.metadata = null; set this.dead = true and return early from play()/show()/startClock() when dead. Keep one module-level 'current audio' for drills: stop it in route() and in Player.play(); give the drill card its own mediaSession play/pause handlers while it is the current audio.

findings.title: Clicking the scrubber inside a different part always lands at the start of that part; the bar shows the clicked position until Play, then snaps back
findings.detail: seekTotal() does show(k).then(() => seekIn(within)). show() has just assigned audio.src, so readyState is 0 and seekIn() skips the audio seek (guard readyState > 0) but still sets this.t and redraws the bar at the clicked position. The audio then starts from 0 and the first timeupdate moves the bar back. Seeking only works inside the part that is already loaded, or in lessons without audio. Also .then runs even when that show() was superseded, so a drag across several parts applies stale offsets.
findings.evidence: node qa/site_review_scratch/player_tests.mjs (the real player.js in Node on a minimal fake DOM and a fake audio element that follows the HTML rules for play()/pause()/src: a pending play() promise rejects with AbortError when src changes or pause() is called). No real browser was used, so the browser half is by specification, the player half is executed code. Scenario D: 'asked for 1.62s (part 2 at 0.42s) -> part 2, shown position p.t=0.42, audio.currentTime=0.00'; 120 ms after Play 'shown p.t=0.10'.
findings.fix: Carry the offset into show(): async show(i, autoplay = this.playing, startAt = 0) { ... if (seg.src) { this.audio.src = seg.src; if (startAt) this.audio.addEventListener('loadedmetadata', () => { if (token === this.token) this.audio.currentTime = Math.min(this.audio.duration - 0.2, (startAt / this.durs[i]) * this.audio.duration); }, { once: true }); } this.tick(startAt); ... } and call this.show(k, this.playing, within) from seekTotal().

findings.title: If widgets.json fails to load the lesson stops dead at the widget part; if it loads late it replaces the slide of a later part
findings.detail: (1) renderWidget awaits ctx.widgets() outside its try. A failed fetch (offline, a 5xx, or an expired session, which returns the login page as HTML so .json() throws) rejects renderVisual, so Player.show() dies before it mounts a slide, switches the clip, calls onSegment or play(). Result when part N-1 ends: i has advanced, playing is true, the Pause icon shows, the previous slide stays up, nothing plays, and the rejection is unhandled. Ten lessons have a widget part. (2) renderVisual mounts into the host itself (visuals.js:199) and show() assigns this.slide before its token check (player.js:100). With the 95 KB widgets.json still in flight on the first widget of a session, skipping ahead or dragging the scrubber across the widget part lets the stale call finish later and put the widget slide on stage while the audio, captions and cues belong to another part.
findings.evidence: node qa/site_review_scratch/player_tests.mjs (the real player.js in Node on a minimal fake DOM and a fake audio element that follows the HTML rules for play()/pause()/src: a pending play() promise rejects with AbortError when src changes or pause() is called). No real browser was used, so the browser half is by specification, the player half is executed code. Scenario F: '[unhandled rejection] TypeError: Failed to fetch' then 'i=1 playing=true audio.paused=true src=seg0.mp3 | onSegment calls: 0 | slide on stage: S0'. Scenario G: 'current part i=2; slide on stage before the data arrived: S2; after: W'.
findings.fix: widgets.js: wrap the whole body in try/catch and return the 'This interactive could not be drawn.' note on any failure. visuals.js: build and return the slide without mounting it. player.js: const slide = await renderVisual(seg.visual, this.ctx).catch(() => fallbackSlide(seg)); if (token !== this.token) return; this.host.replaceChildren(slide); this.slide = slide;

findings.title: The passphrase guess brake is per isolate and per address, resets itself after 5,000 addresses, and then throws; the generated passphrase is about 35 bits, not 'long and random'
findings.detail: tries is a module-level Map: each Cloudflare isolate and location has its own, an IPv6 client can use a new address per request (8 guesses each), and throttled() clears the whole map once it holds more than 5,000 addresses - after which login() runs tries.get(ip).push(...) on undefined and throws (HTTP 500 / error 1101) for every wrong attempt already in flight. A cleared map also un-blocks every throttled address. The 400 ms sleep does not limit parallel requests. deploy.sh builds the passphrase from 5 of 55 words plus two digits: 55^5 * 90 = 4.5e10 combinations (35.4 bits). On the free plan the 100,000 requests/day ceiling is the real limit on guessing - and a guessing run that hits it takes the site down for the day. The owner at the same address as an attacker is locked out too (a correct passphrase gets 429 while throttled).
findings.evidence: node qa/site_review_scratch/worker_tests.mjs (the real worker.js fetch handler in-process, in-memory KV): 'throttle same ip' 303 x8 then 429, right passphrase while throttled 429; 'throttle map overflow' 5003 requests from distinct addresses -> 4986 threw 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading push)'; afterwards the previously throttled address gets 303,303,303 again. node qa/site_review_scratch/misc_tests.mjs: 55 words, 35.4 bits.
findings.fix: Count failures globally instead of per address in memory: a KV counter (key fails:<10-minute bucket>, TTL 20 min; refuse when over ~30) or the Workers Rate Limiting binding keyed on a constant, plus one Cloudflare WAF rate-limit rule on POST /login. Fix the crash: (tries.get(ip) ?? tries.set(ip, []).get(ip)).push(Date.now()) and evict oldest entries instead of clear(). Generate 6 words from the EFF 7,776-word list (77 bits). Longer term, use Cloudflare Access, which the worker already supports.

findings.title: A session cannot be revoked: the cookie lives 180 days, survives a passphrase change, and sign-out only deletes it in that browser
findings.detail: The cookie is exp + HMAC(SESSION_SECRET, 'owner.' + exp). Nothing ties it to the passphrase or to a server-side record, so if the passphrase leaks and is changed, every cookie already issued keeps working until its own expiry; a cookie copied from a browser profile keeps working after 'Sign out'. The only kill switch is rotating SESSION_SECRET by hand, which deploy.sh never does once the secret exists. /logout is also a plain GET that needs no session, so any page can sign the learner out with a link or redirect (nuisance only).
findings.evidence: node qa/site_review_scratch/worker_tests.mjs (the real worker.js fetch handler in-process, in-memory KV): cookie -> valid 200, expiryTampered 401, stillValidAfterPassphraseChange 200, lifetimeDays 180; logout -> 'none - the old cookie value still works'.
findings.fix: Derive the signing key from both secrets, e.g. hmac(env.SESSION_SECRET + '.' + env.PASSPHRASE, ...), so changing the passphrase ends all sessions; shorten SESSION_DAYS to 30 and re-issue the cookie on use when less than half is left. Make sign-out a POST form (SameSite=Lax then blocks cross-site use). Document 'wrangler secret put SESSION_SECRET' as the emergency sign-out-everywhere.

findings.title: The lesson scrubber is announced as a slider and takes focus but cannot be operated from the keyboard
findings.detail: role='slider' tabindex=0 with only pointer handlers. Player.key() deliberately ignores ArrowLeft/ArrowRight and Space when focus is inside [role=slider] (lines 193-195) and the element has no keydown handler of its own, so with focus on it the arrow keys do nothing at all. There is no aria-valuetext, so a screen reader reads raw seconds ('137') with no total. Keyboard users can still move part by part with the two buttons, but not within a part.
findings.evidence: By reading player.js:69-72 and 189-198.
findings.fix: this.scrub.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => { const step = e.key === 'ArrowRight' ? 5 : e.key === 'ArrowLeft' ? -5 : e.key === 'PageUp' ? 30 : e.key === 'PageDown' ? -30 : 0; const now = +this.scrub.getAttribute('aria-valuenow'); if (e.key === 'Home') this.seekTotal(0); else if (e.key === 'End') this.seekTotal(this.total - 1); else if (step) this.seekTotal(Math.max(0, Math.min(this.total - 0.5, now + step))); else return; e.preventDefault(); }); and in tick(): this.scrub.setAttribute('aria-valuetext', clock(before) + ' of ' + clock(this.total));  (needs the seek fix above to be useful across parts).

findings.title: Opening a lesson keeps the previous page's scroll position, so a lesson opened from far down the course map (or the glossary) appears scrolled to its bottom
findings.detail: route() ends with if (name !== 'lesson') scrollTo({ top: 0 }). A fragment navigation to #/lesson/5-3 does not scroll by itself (no element has that id), so after main.replaceChildren(view) the window keeps its old scrollY, clamped to the new page height. From module 5 on the course map, from a 'Lesson 5-3' link at the bottom of the glossary, or from 'Rewatch the lesson' in a review, the learner lands at the bottom of the lesson (the tutor box) instead of the title and steps; for a finished lesson that is the bottom of the long take-away page. Only tab switches inside a lesson scroll to the top (go()). Related: choosing a daily cap calls route(), which jumps from the Settings card at the bottom of #/about back to the top of the page.
findings.evidence: By reading app.js:369-378 and 156 (no browser was allowed).
findings.fix: Always scroll on a route change: remove the condition (go() uses replaceState and does not pass through route()). For the daily-cap buttons update aria-pressed in place instead of calling route().

findings.title: Nothing checks what was deployed: no test that the live site is closed, and the build accepts a lesson with no audio (lesson 4-4 today)
findings.detail: (1) deploy.sh ends by printing the URL. It never requests it, so a wrong binding, a missing secret, an assets setting that bypasses the worker, or a regression in the allow-list would go live unnoticed. (2) build_site.py sets audio to null when a lesson's clips are incomplete and carries on: the current course.json has 37 lessons, 36 with audio - lesson 4-4 would ship as a silent reading-pace lesson whose listening mode still says 'Everything you need is in the audio'. (3) All local testing ran on build/dev_server.mjs, which differs from the real runtime where it matters: it fakes Range support, decodes %2f before resolving the path (an auth bypass that exists only there), serves /login.html without the 307 the asset server sends, and listens on all network interfaces with the passphrase 'test'. (4) 23 superseded clips (6 MB) under site/public/audio are no longer referenced and are uploaded anyway.
findings.evidence: node one-liner over site/public/data/course.json: 'no audio: 4-4 (9 segments)'; 'audio files on disk not referenced by course.json: 23 (6 MB)'. Run before the memory limit stopped it: the real worker under local workerd (wrangler 4.166.0 dev, config qa/site_review_scratch/wrangler.jsonc, port 8799) probed with curl. showed the differences in (3).
findings.fix: Append a smoke test to deploy.sh and fail loudly: for p in / /data/course.json /js/app.js /audio/1-1/x.mp3 '/fonts/..%2fdata/course.json'; do code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --path-as-is "$url$p"); case $code in 303|404) ;; *) echo "OPEN OR BROKEN: $p -> $code"; exit 4;; esac; done; test "$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "$url/api/progress")" = 401; then sign in with the passphrase and check that / returns 200 with a content-security-policy header and that an mp3 answers a Range request with 206. In build_site.py exit non-zero when has_audio != len(lessons) unless --allow-missing. Prune audio files that the manifest does not name. Run the same smoke test against 'wrangler dev' before deploying.

findings.title: The public allow-list is a prefix test on the raw path; on the Node harness '/fonts/..%2fdata/course.json' returns the whole course without a session
findings.detail: open = PUBLIC.has(path) || path.startsWith('/fonts/') decides before the asset layer interprets the path. The harness's ASSETS.fetch does decodeURIComponent then path.join, so '/fonts/..%2fdata/course.json', '/fonts/%2e%2e%2fdata%2fcourse.json' and '/fonts/..%5cdata/course.json' resolve to data/course.json and are served with 200 to anyone. The real asset server looks the decoded path up literally in its manifest and returns 404, so production is not affected today - but the worker's safety rests on that implementation detail, and anything ever placed under public/fonts/ is public. The harness also checks file.startsWith(PUBLIC) without a separator (a sibling folder named public-something would be readable) and listens on every interface.
findings.evidence: curl --path-as-is against the harness on :8788 (while it was running): '/fonts/..%2fdata/course.json 200 application/json size=817146', and the same for ..%2Fdata%2Fcourse.json, %2e%2e%2fdata%2fcourse.json and ..%5cdata/course.json. The same requests and six more encoded variants against workerd on :8799 all gave 404.
findings.fix: const open = PUBLIC.has(path) || /^\/fonts\/[a-z0-9-]+\.woff2$/.test(path); and before anything else: if (/%2f|%5c|%2e|\\|\/\.\.?(\/|$)/i.test(path)) return new Response('Bad path', { status: 400 }). In dev_server.mjs do not decode the path (or reject a decoded path that contains '..'), compare with PUBLIC + path.sep, and listen on 127.0.0.1.

findings.title: The login page, redirects and API responses carry none of the security headers
findings.detail: login() returns env.ASSETS.fetch('/login.html') directly, and the 303/401/JSON responses are built without the header block at lines 146-151. So the one page that takes the passphrase has no Content-Security-Policy, no X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors (it can be framed) and no nosniff, and is served 'Cache-Control: public, max-age=0, must-revalidate'.
findings.evidence: Run before the memory limit stopped it: the real worker under local workerd (wrangler 4.166.0 dev, config qa/site_review_scratch/wrangler.jsonc, port 8799) probed with curl. 'curl -i /login' -> 200 with only Content-Type, Cache-Control: public..., ETag. node qa/site_review_scratch/worker_tests.mjs (the real worker.js fetch handler in-process, in-memory KV): headers /login -> csp false, xfo null.
findings.fix: Move the header block into a helper secure(res, { open }) and wrap every response the worker returns (login page, redirects, JSON). For /login add 'cache-control: no-store'.

findings.title: Error responses for media are cached for a day
findings.detail: Cache-Control is chosen from the path extension alone, so a 404 (or any other status) for an .mp3/.svg/.png gets 'private, max-age=86400'. A clip that was missing or failed once is remembered by the browser for 24 hours; the player answers a failed clip by silently using its clock, so that part stays mute for a day even after the file is fixed.
findings.evidence: Run before the memory limit stopped it: the real worker under local workerd (wrangler 4.166.0 dev, config qa/site_review_scratch/wrangler.jsonc, port 8799) probed with curl. 'curl -i /audio/1-1/00.mp3' (does not exist) -> '404, Cache-Control: private, max-age=86400'. Also in node qa/site_review_scratch/worker_tests.mjs (the real worker.js fetch handler in-process, in-memory KV).
findings.fix: if (!open) h.set('cache-control', res.ok && /\.(mp3|woff2|png|jpg|svg)$/.test(path) ? 'private, max-age=31536000, immutable' : 'private, no-cache');  (the clip names are content-hashed, so a year is safe for 200s) and 'no-store' for non-2xx.

findings.title: Access mode: a token without exp is accepted, nbf is ignored, every unknown kid costs a certs fetch, and a certs outage locks everyone out even with keys in memory
findings.detail: body.exp * 1000 < Date.now() is false when exp is missing (NaN), nbf/iat/iss are never read. The certs are re-fetched whenever the kid is unknown, so 25 requests with made-up tokens cause 25 outbound fetches (no negative caching, unauthenticated). If the certs fetch throws after the one-hour cache age, the catch returns null before the cached keys are consulted, so valid users get 401 until the endpoint is back. Signature, audience and algorithm handling are sound (RS256 is forced, alg none / HS256 / tampered body are rejected). Also: the KV key changes from progress:owner to progress:<email> when Access is switched on, so server-side progress appears empty until a browser that still has it locally syncs; and in Access mode 'Sign out' leads to a passphrase form that cannot work.
findings.evidence: node qa/site_review_scratch/worker_tests.mjs (the real worker.js fetch handler in-process, in-memory KV) section 7: noExpClaim '200 a@b.c', notYetValid_nbf '200 a@b.c', algNone/hs256/tamperedBody/wrongAud/expired 401; 'certs fetches caused by 25 unauthenticated requests with unknown kid: 25'; 'valid token while the certs endpoint is down (cache older than 1h): 401'; kv key 'progress:learner@example.com'.
findings.fix: Require typeof body.exp === 'number', reject nbf > now + 60 s, check body.iss === 'https://' + env.ACCESS_TEAM + '.cloudflareaccess.com'. Refresh keys at most once a minute for unknown kids and keep the old set when the fetch fails. On the first authenticated request in Access mode, if progress:<email> is empty and progress:owner exists, copy it. Hide 'Sign out' (or link to /cdn-cgi/access/logout) when /api/me reports an e-mail user.

findings.title: The 512 KB body limit counts UTF-16 units after the whole body has been read
findings.detail: content-length is optional (chunked uploads have none) and the fallback compares text.length, so an 819 KB body of two-byte characters is accepted, and any size is fully buffered before the check. Only a signed-in client can do this; the stored document can also grow without bound across many PUTs because only the incoming half is measured.
findings.evidence: node qa/site_review_scratch/worker_tests.mjs (the real worker.js fetch handler in-process, in-memory KV): '800KB body, no content-length (chunked): status 200, bytes 819245, limit 524288'.
findings.fix: Read with a cap: const buf = await req.arrayBuffer(); if (buf.byteLength > MAX_BODY) return 413; const text = new TextDecoder().decode(buf); and refuse to store when JSON.stringify(merged).length > 2 * MAX_BODY.

findings.title: The tutor address is not validated, is synced to every device, and receives each question with the lesson text and the typed answer
findings.detail: Any string is stored as claudeUrl and used as window.open(base + '?q=' + ...). A typo or a pasted non-Claude address sends the prompts (including what the learner typed in 'Explain') to that site from every device, and a javascript: or data: value is passed to window.open (blocked only by the CSP of the opener). Only the signed-in learner can set it, so this is a foot-gun rather than an attack path.
findings.evidence: By reading app.js:69-70 and 361.
findings.fix: On change: let u; try { u = new URL(value); } catch {} if (value && !(u && u.protocol === 'https:' && u.hostname === 'claude.ai')) { toast('That is not a claude.ai address'); return; }  and apply the same test again in askClaude() before opening.

findings.title: Two devices saving at the same moment: the server keeps only one of them (read-merge-write on KV is not atomic)
findings.detail: Both PUTs read the same stored document, each merges its own records and writes; the second write wins. Each device is told its own data is saved. The loser's records are missing on the server until that device pushes again (its next change or page load), which it normally does - but if its browser storage is cleared first, they are gone. KV's eventual consistency between locations widens the window to about a minute.
findings.evidence: node qa/site_review_scratch/race_test.mjs (KV get/put delayed 20 ms): phone told 'base,fromPhone', laptop told 'base,fromLaptop', server actually has 'base,fromLaptop'.
findings.fix: Acceptable for one learner if the client re-syncs when a tab becomes visible (see the keepalive finding). The robust fix is a Durable Object (one per user, SQLite storage) that serialises GET/PUT; the merge function stays the same.

findings.title: Two tabs in one browser overwrite each other's local copy
findings.detail: Every tab keeps its own in-memory state and local.write() stores that whole state under one key; there is no 'storage' listener and no read-merge before writing. Offline (or before the 4-20 s push), a lesson finished in tab 1 disappears from localStorage as soon as tab 2, opened earlier, records anything; if tab 1 is then closed its work exists nowhere.
findings.evidence: node qa/site_review_scratch/store_tests.mjs (the real store.js, one module instance per simulated device, against the real worker.js, with a controllable clock) section 5: localStorage after tab1 finished a lesson 'lessons [1-1] cards [1-1-c0]'; after tab2 does anything 'lessons [1-2] cards []'.
findings.fix: write() { state = merge(state, local.read()); localStorage.setItem(KEY, JSON.stringify(state)); } and addEventListener('storage', (e) => { if (e.key === KEY) { state = merge(state, local.read()); emit(); } }).

findings.title: 'Start over' also deletes the settings, and progress is tied to the browser rather than the signed-in person
findings.detail: resetAll() replaces settings with { t, reset }, so the saved Claude Project address and the daily cap are lost with the progress. Separately, the local copy uses one fixed key and is not cleared at sign-out: on a shared computer the previous learner's progress stays readable in localStorage and is merged into whoever signs in next (it matters only if Access mode is ever used with more than one address).
findings.evidence: node qa/site_review_scratch/store_tests.mjs (the real store.js, one module instance per simulated device, against the real worker.js, with a controllable clock) section 6: settings after Start over = {t, reset}. The second part by reading store.js:4 and the /logout handler.
findings.fix: state.settings = { ...state.settings, t: Date.now(), reset: Date.now() }. Key the local copy by user (KEY + ':' + user from /api/me) and remove it on sign-out after a final successful push.

findings.title: Day arithmetic uses 24-hour steps: a card missed at 23:50 is due again at 00:05, a card answered in the first hour of the day the clocks go back is due again at once, and the 7-day strip skips a day after the clocks go forward
findings.detail: dueAt() adds N*24h and then sets 04:00, but due() treats everything up to 23:59:59 today as due, so the review day rolls over at midnight and the 04:00 has no effect: a late session that crosses midnight gets the cards it just answered wrong (and the daily cap is refilled at the same moment). On a 25-hour day (the night the clocks go back) now+24h is still the same calendar date, so a card answered at 00:30 is due the same day. stats().week walks back in 24-hour steps, so between 00:00 and 01:00 in the week after a 23-hour day one date is skipped and an eighth is shown.
findings.evidence: node qa/site_review_scratch/store_tests.mjs (the real store.js, one module instance per simulated device, against the real worker.js, with a controllable clock) section 7 (TZ=Asia/Jerusalem): 'answered wrong at 23:50 -> due 2026-11-26 04:00; at 00:05 (15 minutes later) it is due again: true'; 'answered right at 2026-10-25 00:30 -> due 2026-10-25 04:00 | due again immediately: true'; strip on 2027-03-28 00:30 = '03-21 03-22 03-23 03-24 03-25 03-27 03-28' (03-26 missing).
findings.fix: Use calendar arithmetic with one roll-over hour for everything: const studyDay = (ms = Date.now()) => { const d = new Date(ms - 4 * 3600e3); d.setHours(0, 0, 0, 0); return d; }; dueAt = (box) => { const d = studyDay(); d.setDate(d.getDate() + INTERVALS[box]); d.setHours(4); return d.getTime(); }; 'due' means due <= now-day's end computed from studyDay(); build the week strip with setDate(getDate() - i).

findings.title: Leftover '|| true': pressing Next on the last part marks the lesson watched and credits its minutes without anything having played
findings.detail: if (!manual || this.t > 0 || true) is always true, so ArrowRight held down from the start reaches onComplete in a second: watched is stored, 'minutes watched' grows by the full lesson, and the quiz can then complete the lesson. Pressing Play after the end fires onComplete again each time. If skipping is meant to be allowed, the completion rule in the 'never marked done' finding should not depend on watched at all.
findings.evidence: node qa/site_review_scratch/player_tests.mjs (the real player.js in Node on a minimal fake DOM and a fake audio element that follows the HTML rules for play()/pause()/src: a pending play() promise rejects with AbortError when src changes or pause() is called). No real browser was used, so the browser half is by specification, the player half is executed code. Scenario I: 'onComplete calls (lesson marked watched): 1 | played: false'; Scenario J: complete calls go 1 -> 2 on Play after the end.
findings.fix: Decide the rule and write it plainly, e.g. count a lesson as watched when the last part ENDS (not manual), or when at least 80% of the parts have ended; call onComplete once (guard with this.completed).

findings.title: Review counters go stale or mislead: the header badge is only recomputed on navigation, and cards whose question no longer exists make the empty state say 'You have hit today's cap'
findings.detail: The due badge is set in route() only, so after a review session it keeps showing the old number until the next navigation. review() decides 'capped' from store.due().length, which also counts cards whose lesson or concept has been removed from course.json (cardQuestion() returns null for them and dueQueue() drops them), so after a content change the page claims the cap was hit, forever, instead of 'Nothing due today'. cardQuestion() also throws on a card id with fewer than three parts (c.slice on undefined) - reachable only through a hand-edited or corrupted state.
findings.evidence: By reading app.js:239-255 and 375-376.
findings.fix: Recompute the badge in a store.onChange handler; const capped = store.due().some((c) => cardQuestion(c)); let cardQuestion return null unless /^\d+-\d+-c\d+$/.test(cid) or it starts with 't-'.

findings.title: After a widget part the lesson does not resume: 'Done exploring - continue' shows the next part paused, and the main Play button replays the widget part or does nothing
findings.detail: segmentEnded() pauses on a widget part and shows the continue button, whose handler is next(true); next() passes this.playing (false) as autoplay, so the next slide appears paused with no overlay or hint. Pressing the main Play button (or Space) instead calls audio.play() on the ended clip, which restarts the same narration from 0; on the silent clock it ends again immediately. The button also sits on the same spot as the caption line.
findings.evidence: node qa/site_review_scratch/player_tests.mjs (the real player.js in Node on a minimal fake DOM and a fake audio element that follows the HTML rules for play()/pause()/src: a pending play() promise rejects with AbortError when src changes or pause() is called). No real browser was used, so the browser half is by specification, the player half is executed code. Scenario H: when the widget part's audio ended 'playing=false | continue button hidden: false'; after 'Done exploring - continue' 'i=2 playing=false audio.paused=true'. The replay half is by reading.
findings.fix: Continue button: onclick: () => this.show(this.i + 1, true) (or onComplete when it is the last part). In play(): if (!this.moreEl.hidden) return this.next(true) with autoplay forced.

findings.title: Captions break inside decimal numbers: 131 places such as 'Below 0.' / '7 means spend is down...'
findings.detail: The sentence splitter treats every full stop as an end of sentence. The narration contains 123 decimal numbers, so with CC on the caption shows 'Is 0.' and then '7 really the best cut-off?'; 52 caption fragments are shorter than four characters. Captions are the only text alternative during playback, so this lands on exactly the learners who rely on them.
findings.evidence: node qa/site_review_scratch/misc_tests.mjs section 1: '311 segments; 131 sentence breaks inside a number/abbreviation; fragments under 4 chars: 52', first examples from lesson 1-1.
findings.fix: End a sentence only where the terminator is followed by whitespace or the end of the text: spoken.match(/.*?[.!?]+["')\]]*(?=\s|$)\s*|.+$/g). Tested on all 311 segments (qa/site_review_scratch/fix_checks.mjs): 2,776 captions, 0 breaks inside a number, 0 fragments under 4 characters, no text lost, longest caption unchanged at 198 characters.

findings.title: End-of-lesson and missing-audio states are invisible: the 'That is the lesson' banner is outside the full-screen element, the full-screen button does nothing on iPhone, and the silent fallback is never announced
findings.detail: onComplete un-hides a banner that lives outside .stage-wrap, so in full screen the lesson just stops on the last slide. requestFullscreen does not exist on iPhone Safari for non-video elements and the optional call swallows that, leaving a dead button. When a clip fails (or a lesson has no audio, like 4-4 in the current build) the player switches to its clock without any sign, and listening mode still says 'Everything you need is in the audio'.
findings.evidence: By reading player.js:131,160,188 and app.js:174-176.
findings.fix: On complete: if (document.fullscreenElement) document.exitFullscreen(); hide the full-screen button when !this.wrap.requestFullscreen; show a 'No audio for this part - reading pace' chip in the controls while silent, and disable listening mode for parts without src.

findings.title: Scrubbing can stick: only pointerup ends a drag
findings.detail: pointerdown installs onpointermove and only pointerup removes it. A cancelled pointer (system gesture, pen leaving, window switch during a drag) leaves the handler installed, after which merely moving the mouse over the bar seeks continuously.
findings.evidence: By reading player.js:71-72.
findings.fix: const end = () => (this.scrub.onpointermove = null); for (const t of ['pointerup', 'pointercancel', 'lostpointercapture']) this.scrub.addEventListener(t, end);

findings.title: Route and step names are looked up on plain objects, so '#/__proto__' throws and '#/constructor/x' prints 'x'
findings.detail: ROUTES[name] and VIEW[step] find Object.prototype members. #/__proto__, #/hasOwnProperty and #/valueOf throw a TypeError inside route(): on a fresh load boot() dies after 'Loading the course...' and the page never renders; on an in-page navigation the old view stays. #/constructor/x renders the text 'x', #/lesson/1-1/constructor renders '[object Object]' in the panel, #/lesson/1-1/__proto__ throws. Text only, no script execution. Unknown ordinary names are handled correctly (not-found page; unknown step falls back to Guess).
findings.evidence: node qa/site_review_scratch/misc_tests.mjs section 4 (same lookups on objects of the same shape): '#/__proto__ -> TypeError: not a function (object)', '#/constructor -> calls Object -> a', '#/lesson/1-1/constructor -> renders [object Object]', '#/nope -> notFound'.
findings.fix: const pick = (table, key) => (Object.hasOwn(table, key) ? table[key] : null); const view = (pick(ROUTES, name) || notFound)(a, b); if (!pick(VIEW, step)) step = 'guess'; and wrap the body of route() in try/catch that renders notFound().

findings.title: A deep link does not survive sign-in, and a session that ends mid-lesson throws away what was on screen
findings.detail: After a correct passphrase the worker always redirects to '/', and the form posts to /login without the fragment, so https://site/#/lesson/3-2 opened while signed out ends on the home page. In the app, any 401 from /api/progress does location.href = '/login' immediately: quiz answers not yet finished (they are only stored at the end), a typed 'Explain' answer and the place in the course are gone, and the return trip again lands on '/'.
findings.evidence: curl -i -X POST --data-urlencode passphrase=test /login -> '303, Location: /' on both servers; the rest by reading store.js:44,64 and login.html:16.
findings.fix: Serve a tiny public /js/login.js from the login page that copies location.hash into a hidden field 'next'; in the worker accept it only if /^#\/[\w\/-]*$/.test(next) and redirect to '/' + next. In store.js, on 401 keep the page: set a flag, show a 'Signed out - sign in again' bar whose link carries the current hash, and let the user finish reading.

findings.title: First paint waits for /api/progress with no time limit, and a failed boot gives the wrong advice
findings.detail: boot() awaits store.init(), whose fetch has no timeout: on a hanging connection (captive portal, weak signal) the page stays on 'Loading the course...' although the course and the local progress are already in hand. If course.json answers with something that is not JSON (an expired session returns the login page) the message is 'Check your connection and reload'. An exception inside init() or the first route() leaves the loading card up with no message.
findings.evidence: By reading app.js:392-400 and store.js:39-54.
findings.fix: Render first, sync after: state = merge(blank(), local.read()); route(); then init() with fetch(..., { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(8000) }) and re-route when the merged state differs. In the course.json catch, if the response was redirected to /login go there. Wrap boot in try/catch that shows the error card.

findings.title: The tutor prompt is cut from the end, so a long typed answer removes the actual instruction; an emoji on the cut throws; non-Latin text makes a 33 KB address
findings.detail: parts = [who, lesson, extra, question]; .slice(0, 5500) trims the question first. For 'Have Claude grade it' a typed answer longer than about 3,600 characters pushes 'My question: Grade my answer...' out, and Claude receives context with no request. If the cut lands inside a surrogate pair encodeURIComponent throws URIError after the clipboard copy, and no tab opens. 5,500 non-Latin characters encode to 33,000 bytes of URL, which claude.ai's front door is likely to refuse. With normal use there is room: the longest lesson context leaves 3,710 characters.
findings.evidence: node qa/site_review_scratch/misc_tests.mjs section 2: 'room left for the typed question at worst: 3710'; 'a typed answer longer than 3595 chars ... pushes the instruction off the end'; 'emoji at the cut -> URIError: URI malformed'; 'URL length for 5,500 non-Latin chars: 33000 bytes'.
findings.fix: Trim the context, never the question: const tail = '\nMy question: ' + ask; const head = [WHO, lessonPart, extra].join(''); const q = Array.from(head).slice(0, 5500 - tail.length).join('') + tail; and cap by encoded size: while (encodeURIComponent(q).length > 12000) shorten the head. The full text is on the clipboard anyway, so say so in the toast when it was shortened.

findings.title: With 'reduce motion' on, the listening-mode wave becomes a flicker instead of stopping
findings.detail: The reduced-motion rule shortens every animation to .01 ms but leaves animation-iteration-count alone. '.listen .wave i' (line 406) runs 'wave 1.1s ease-in-out infinite', so under the preference the five bars restart 100,000 times a second and are painted at a random height on every frame while a lesson plays in listening mode - for exactly the people who asked for less motion. JS-driven smooth scrolling (scrollIntoView({ behavior: 'smooth' })) is not covered by the rule either.
findings.evidence: By reading app.css:406 and 552.
findings.fix: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { *, *::before, *::after { animation-duration: .01ms !important; animation-iteration-count: 1 !important; transition-duration: .01ms !important; scroll-behavior: auto !important; } .listen .wave i { animation: none; height: 60%; } }  and pass behavior: matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches ? 'auto' : 'smooth' to scrollIntoView.

findings.title: Contrast: body and muted text pass in both themes, but four spots do not
findings.detail: Computed from the tokens. Passing: --ink-3 on --surface 5.44 (light) / 5.88 (dark), on --bg 4.72 / 6.47, on --surface-2 4.95 / 5.27; --ink-2 7.2 or better everywhere; links 5.2 or better; primary button 6.1 / 8.4. Failing: (1) the letter in the answer chip after answering, white on --good and on --bad in the DARK theme: 2.29 and 2.74 (lines 425, 427); (2) 'written by your assistant - not checked by anyone', --redline on the report bar at .76rem: 3.76 light, 3.44 dark (line 463); (3) table headers inside a case-file report, the report's own --ink-3 (55% mix) on paper: 3.72 / 3.64; (4) non-text: the unplayed part of the scrubber rail against the control bar 1.26 / 1.29, input borders (--line-strong) 1.91 / 1.87, unanswered option borders (--line) 1.45 / 1.33, all under the 3:1 asked of control boundaries. --ink-3 on --surface-3 is 4.32 in light (only matters if used for text there).
findings.evidence: node qa/site_review_scratch/misc_tests.mjs section 5 (WCAG relative-luminance formula over the :root and [data-theme=dark] tokens).
findings.fix: Checked values (qa/site_review_scratch/fix_checks.mjs): add a token --chip-ink (#ffffff in light, #141c1d in dark) and use it in .opt.right i / .opt.wrong i - dark gives 7.55 on --good and 6.31 on --bad; .report .bar em { color: #a33c12; } gives 5.42 / 4.95; .report { --ink-3: color-mix(in srgb, var(--paper-ink) 65%, var(--paper)); } gives 5.09 / 4.92; for the scrubber rail, input borders and option borders use color-mix(in srgb, var(--ink-3) 75%, var(--surface)), which is 3.25 light / 3.91 dark.

findings.title: Single-letter shortcuts are always on: A-D / 1-4 answer a question from anywhere on the page, irreversibly
findings.detail: The new window-level keydown handler answers the visible question on a bare a/b/c/d/1/2/3/4 unless focus is in an input; the player does the same with c and f. There is no way to switch them off or remap them (WCAG 2.1.4), which is the case speech-input users hit: a dictated word is typed as letters. In the daily review a stray key is not just a wrong mark - store.answer() runs at once and sends the card back to box 0 with no undo. The handler also assumes e.key is a string and e.target an element (both can be otherwise for synthetic events), and the hint 'Keys: A to D to answer, Enter to go on' is hidden on touch devices but the keys stay live for a paired keyboard.
findings.evidence: By reading app.js:382-388 and player.js:189-198.
findings.fix: Add a 'Keyboard shortcuts' switch in Settings (prefs, default on) and check it in both handlers; ignore e.repeat and events whose target is not an Element; in the review, offer 'Undo' on the feedback line until Next is pressed (apply store.answer on Next instead of on the key).

findings.title: Semantics: the lesson steps claim to be tabs but are not, quiz feedback is not announced, and a route change does not move focus
findings.detail: The step bar is ol[role=tablist] > li > button[role=tab]: the li breaks the required tablist-tab ownership, there is no tabpanel or aria-controls, all five are in the tab order and arrow keys do not move between them (in Watch they skip parts instead). After an answer the 'Right.' / 'Not quite' text appears in a div with no live region while focus jumps to the Next button, so a screen-reader user hears only 'Next question'. route() replaces the main content and scrolls, but focus stays on the link that was clicked and nothing is announced. Smaller: the 'Explain' textarea and the tutor-address field have no label; the 7-day strip and quiz progress bars are bare <i> elements; focusable bar rows and chart hit areas sit inside role=img; controls under the start overlay and under the listening screen stay focusable.
findings.fix: Steps: <nav aria-label='Lesson steps'> with plain buttons and aria-current='step'. Feedback: why.setAttribute('role', 'status') before filling it, or move focus to it (tabindex=-1) and let Enter go on. Route: give the new view's h1 tabindex=-1 and focus it. Add aria-label to the textarea and the url input, role='img' + aria-label ('Studied 3 of the last 7 days') to the strip, and inert on the slide host while the overlay or listening screen covers it.

findings.title: Small or unreachable targets: the 40 px rule for the phone's previous/next buttons names a class that does not exist; the 'Show the numbers' link and the 'optional' label are tiny; transcript paragraphs are click-only
findings.detail: '.controls .left .btn-ic' matches nothing (the buttons carry .icon-btn), so previous/next stay 36 px on phones. .data-toggle is .72em text with no padding (about 12 px tall in a slide), under the 24 px minimum. '.steps button small' is .78em of .72rem on phones, about 9 px. Transcript paragraphs jump the lesson to their part on click but have no role, tabindex or key handler. The toast sits at bottom: 22px without env(safe-area-inset-bottom).
findings.evidence: node qa/site_review_scratch/misc_tests.mjs section 6: 'css class btn-ic used in JS: false | in CSS: true'; the sizes by reading app.css:71, 184, 322, 411, 518, 525.
findings.fix: .controls .left .icon-btn { width: 44px; height: 44px; } inside the phone block; .data-toggle { padding: 6px 0; min-height: 24px; font-size: max(.72em, 12px); }; render transcript parts as <button class='tr-part'> elements; .toast { bottom: calc(22px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px)); }.

findings.title: The 'not signed in' guard only works while wrangler whoami exits 0
findings.detail: The line is 'whoami | grep -qi "not authenticated" && { ...; exit 2; }' under set -o pipefail. If whoami ever exits non-zero when signed out (its --json form already does, and grep -q closing the pipe early can make wrangler fail on its next write), the pipeline is 'failed', the && block is skipped and, being the left side of &&, set -e does not stop the script: it builds and then fails later with 'Could not create or find the KV namespace', which sends the owner looking in the wrong place. With wrangler 4.166.0 the plain command prints the message and exits 0, so it works today.
findings.evidence: bash -c 'set -euo pipefail; (echo "You are not authenticated."; exit 1) | grep -qi "not authenticated" && { echo GUARD; exit 2; }; echo continues' prints 'continues' (rc 0); with exit 0 it prints GUARD. node_modules/wrangler/wrangler-dist/cli.js whoami(): logs the message and returns when not --json.
findings.fix: who=$($W whoami 2>&1 || true); if grep -qi 'not authenticated' <<<"$who"; then echo 'Not signed in to Cloudflare. Run cf-login.cmd first.'; exit 2; fi

findings.title: The deploy log with the site address is written to a tracked folder, and the script dies silently at the end if that address is not found
findings.detail: qa/deploy.log is not in .gitignore (only qa/shots, qa/labs_scratch and qa/voices are), so the workers.dev address and account subdomain get committed, while the script takes care to keep the same address in the ignored .secrets/url.txt. With the address public, the passphrase is the only thing between the internet and the course. Separately, url=$(grep -o ... | tail -1) under set -euo pipefail aborts the script without a message when the log has no workers.dev line (custom domain, changed output), after everything was deployed and before 'Deployed:' is printed. If 'secret list' fails transiently, have=[] makes the script overwrite SESSION_SECRET (signing everyone out) and re-put the passphrase.
findings.evidence: bash -c 'set -euo pipefail; url=$(echo "no url here" | grep -o "https://[a-z0-9.-]*workers.dev" | tail -1); echo Deployed' -> no output, rc 1. .gitignore read: no qa/deploy.log entry.
findings.fix: tee ../.secrets/deploy.log instead; url=$(grep -o 'https://[a-z0-9.-]*workers.dev' ../.secrets/deploy.log | tail -1 || true); [ -n "$url" ] || echo 'Deployed, but no workers.dev address was printed'. have=$($W secret list) || { echo 'Could not list secrets; not touching them'; exit 5; }

checked_ok: Auth fails closed: with PASSPHRASE and/or SESSION_SECRET unset or empty every login is refused and a forged cookie gets the login redirect (worker_tests section 1).

On the real runtime (workerd) no protected asset or API path is served without a session. Of 35 unauthenticated probes, the 14 protected paths (/, /index.html, /data/course.json, /js/app.js, //data/course.json, /DATA/course.json, /data/course.json., /Login.html, /login/, /fonts/../data/course.json, /fonts/%2e%2e/data/course.json, an encoded path under /login.html, /cdn-cgi/x, /logout) redirected to /login, the two API paths gave 401, and 12 odd paths under /fonts/ (ten %2f / %5c / %252e encodings, a double slash, the bare directory) gave 404. Only /login, the two stylesheets, mark.svg, favicon.svg and the font files answered 200.

Session cookie: HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Path=/; the expiry is inside the signature (changing it gives 401); comparison is constant-time over the longer length; an expired or malformed cookie is rejected.

CSRF on PUT /api/progress: PUT is never a simple cross-site request, the preflight gets 401 (no cookie) or 405 with no CORS headers, and the Lax cookie is not sent on cross-site subrequests; POST/DELETE give 405. The content-type test is loose ('text/plain; application/json' passes) but is not what the protection rests on.

Access JWT verification: RS256 is forced at importKey, so alg none and HS256 tokens, a tampered body, a wrong audience and an expired token are all rejected; a request without the header gets 401; the passphrase cookie is ignored in Access mode.
No open redirect: every Location the worker sends is a fixed path on the request's own host; there is no next/return parameter.

No HTML injection sink: innerHTML is assigned only static icon constants (app.js 25, 37, 47, 123, 154; player.js 14, 118, 126); all course text, typed text and hash segments reach the DOM through textContent, setAttribute or text nodes; the hash is only compared with lesson ids and route names.

CSP on app responses has no script 'unsafe-inline', no remote origin, base-uri 'none', frame-ancestors 'none', form-action 'self'; index.html has no inline script; referrer-policy same-origin keeps the site address out of claude.ai's logs.
Prototype pollution: a '__proto__' key inside a collection does not reach Object.prototype and is not stored; collection names are a fixed list (worker_tests section 5).

merge() in worker.js and store.js give byte-identical results on 3,000 random well-formed state pairs (store_tests section 1); they differ only for malformed input (the worker drops non-object records and string collections, the client keeps them).
The reset marker survives a newer settings object from another device (max of both sides), and a push that was in flight during a reset cannot bring old records back.
KV key cannot be steered by the user id: it is the literal 'owner' or the e-mail from a verified token; backup keys use a different prefix.

Spaced repetition: intervals 1/3/7/14/30/60 days, capped at box 5; a wrong answer returns to box 0 and keeps n/ok; seed() never overwrites an existing card; every review concept has exactly 3 variants so n % variants.length is safe; stats() has no division by zero on an empty course or with no answers.

Course data matches what the code assumes: 37 lessons, each with 4 quiz questions of at most 4 options, 2 review concepts, 3 takeaways and at least one segment; all 312 referenced clips and 7 drill files exist; case-file marks point at existing report blocks and only real findings carry marks; no file exceeds the 25 MiB asset limit (99 MB, 350 files in total).

Player housekeeping that is right: the window keydown listener is removed in destroy() and ignores input, textarea, select and contenteditable; destroy() is called on every route change and step change; the show() token stops a superseded call from touching audio or cues; the fit() loops are bounded (at most 10 steps down, 9 up) and neither fit() nor the measure class changes the observed stage size, so the ResizeObserver cannot loop.
Playback rate is re-applied after every src change and in play(), is honoured by the silent clock, and a stored speed that is no longer in the list falls back cleanly.
State size: a finished course with a year of daily use serialises to about 27 KB, under the 64 KB keepalive limit and the 512 KB server limit.

Sign-in works on the real runtime although the asset server redirects /login.html to /login: the binding fetch follows the 307 (workerd: GET /login 200; wrong passphrase -> /login?wrong=1#wrong; correct -> / with the cookie).
Conditional and compressed responses pass through the header wrapper intact on workerd (304 with ETag, HEAD, gzip).

deploy.sh: neither secret is echoed (wrangler output is discarded, only the file path is printed); the passphrase lives only in the git-ignored .secrets/; the KV list/create parsing matches wrangler 4.166.0's actual output and its config prompt falls back to 'no' without a terminal; the first deploy, before the secrets exist, is closed.
.dev transport: workers.dev is HTTPS-only and the .dev TLD is HSTS-preloaded, so the missing Strict-Transport-Security header matters only if a custom domain is added.
not_checked: No real browser was run (not allowed in this pass): every finding marked confirmed:false, and the browser half of the player findings, rests on reading the code and on the HTML specification.

Production Cloudflare was not touched: behaviour of the edge in front of the worker (Range handling, the free-plan request ceiling, preview URLs) is inferred from local workerd and the wrangler source.
iOS Safari audio behaviour without range support - test one lesson and one drill on the phone immediately after the first deploy.
Line numbers in app.css and app.js are those at 23:50 on 2026-11-21; the owner was still editing those files.
